title: Chapter 715
paragraphs: Chapter 715
Episode 180. Everyone's Battle (5)
If Gilly hadn't become a nanny for Runkandel, and had continued her training as a knight of MacLoran, she could have kept the words she just said.
However, Dox is the Black Knight.
Although his potential is far less than Gilly's, and he is currently in a state of falling into corruption. The weight of the black helmet he wore did not lighten.

Furthermore, the prophet had contributed greatly to Dox's corruption. He allowed him to keep the dignity he had built up as a warrior, while only causing him to fall enough to be consumed by hatred and madness.
In other words, Dox was now able to fully demonstrate his abilities.

[How dare a mere nanny... laughable, Gilly. You should have boasted like that in the old days. After you left the clan, I grew stronger by crossing countless life-or-death situations. The same was true after I wore the black helmet.]
Clang-!
"Ugh!"
Dox's claw struck Gilly. She blocked it, but she couldn't dare to compete in a power struggle.
Her entire wrist was shaking as if it would fall off, forcing her to grit her teeth. With every block of Dox's attack, her entire body was shaking.
But Gilly, with her face twisted in pain, maintained her stance and fixed her gaze on Dox. Her steady claw was wrapped in a brilliant aura.
[Not bad for someone who spent a comfortable time rotting.]
Without pause, Dox's unilateral attack continued. Gilly had to squeeze out her strength every moment, but Dox was relaxed as if he were dealing with a child.
Strength, speed, experience.
There wasn't a single area where Gilly could beat Dox right now. The words she confidently spoke were merely to provoke Dox, even a little, and she was well aware that it was unrealistic.
[That's enough. What on earth are you trying to show me?]
Crack!
The moment Dox finished his sentence, Gilly had to hear the sound of her left wrist twisting. While their claws were entwined, Dox suddenly attacked her wrist with his elbow, breaking her balance.
"Argh…!"
Gilly groaned and quickly stepped to the left. But Dox didn't give her a chance to escape and attacked the same spot again. The broken bone sharply jabbed the inside of her skin again.
[This is the first time I'm hearing your scream.]
"Hah, are you satisfied now?"
[No, I'm disappointed. I thought that you, the monster-like Gilly, would still have something impressive left, no matter how rusty you've gotten.]
"I'm not a monster, just a normal person. The real monsters are you... or rather, those who made you like this."
[But it breaks too easily. To the point of emptiness…]
Dox stopped his attack.

Gilly used the opportunity to increase the distance and hastily wrapped her broken wrist with a bandage. It didn't wrap well as she was conscious of Dox. Cold sweat flowed from her entire body, and her breathing was getting faster.
Sigh...
Dox let out a long sigh. The frail figure before him bore no resemblance to the Gilly he remembered.
Soon, Dox took something out from his pocket and threw it in front of Gilly. She flinched and was about to retaliate when she recognized it was a black pill that had fallen on the ground.
"What is this?"
[It's called Soul Pill, a medicine made by the prophet.]
"If I take this, will I become like you?"

[Temporarily, it rejuvenates the body and causes an explosive surge of energy. Of course, even if you take the Soul Pill, your chances of defeating me are slim, but it's better than dying like this. Above all, I want to see it again. Your old self.]
Gilly, as if there was no value in contemplating, crushed the Soul Pill underfoot.
"I don't need it."
[That's strange. When you were praised as the greatest genius of MacLoran, you seemed to act without any pride, but now you stubbornly refuse, even in the face of death.]
Gilly took a breath and aimed her claw at Dox again.
"When I was hated and ostracized by the clan, I remained silent because I was given the name MacLoran. It wasn't because I had no pride."
[You were never a MacLoran.]

"No matter how the clan and you saw me, I never forgot that I was a MacLoran. Everything I know about the sword, I learned from MacLoran, and all the happiness I have experienced in my life came from what I gained because I was part of MacLoran."
That's why Gilly never told Jin and her companions about her past in MacLoran.
-I'm sorry, sir.
-Why are you sorry?
-My clan is disrespecting you. It's probably because of me.
-It's okay, Gilly. There's no need for you to feel sorry. I don't harbor any hard feelings against MacLoran because of this incident, so don't worry.

Even when Jin became a knight, Gilly sent no representative and instead rudely apologized on behalf of MacLoran. When Dox fell into Jin's clutches, she was worried about what would happen if he was harmed.
Of course, Gilly suffered many wounds during her time in MacLoran. But she thought all that pain was incomparable to what she had gained since leaving the slums.
Jin and Murakan, and the comrades she met while adventuring together since the days of being a squire. They were, in a sense, her family. She would never have had them if not for MacLoran.
The aura around Gilly's claws deepened.
[Are you trying to end this in one go? Good, I'll wait.]
"Do you remember? This is the secret technique of the family that you so desperately wanted to learn."
[MacLoran's 66th... quite a familiar technique.]
"You probably still believe that the 66th was created by the head of the family."
Dox's pupils narrowed.
[...Don't tell me it was you, not father.]

"Yes, it was known as a technique devised by the head, but it was actually something I thought of when I was seventeen. That's why only I know the intricacies of the 66th, which the head could never master."
[Ha, even father felt inferior to you like me. But it's a shame, you should have taken the Soul Pill. With that broken arm, you can't handle the 66th. Anyway, show me. I'll break it straight on.]
As Dox lifted his claws and prepared to receive, Gill lowered his stance. A stance that Dox practiced millions of times until his young adulthood.
'A rush and acceleration, followed by consecutive strikes. The structure is simple, but the distribution of the center is extremely difficult. He came up with this at seventeen...'
Then Gill rushed towards Dox with a shout.
If Dox had decided the fight before the technique started, it would have been different, but once the 66th started, even Dox had no choice but to momentarily give Gill the initiative.
However, Dox was perfectly parrying Gill's claws. Even if he didn't know the 66th at all, he would have only left a few afterimages at most, let alone a technique he was so familiar with.
'Three consecutive strikes here, then downward, then rotation and position change when he blocks or dodges.'

Now the 66th was a technique that Dox had fully mastered. That's why Gill was taking even more damage while aggressively attacking. Because of the overflow of aura caused by the excessive use of his injured body.
'It's a technique that inherently causes overflow, and it's remarkable that he managed this much with his broken arm. Is it the end now?'
If Gill really created the 66th, only the end would be different.
The end of the 66th that Dox knew was evasion. If the opponent was still alive after all the strikes of the 66th, he had to retreat.
Therefore, the 66th was a precarious technique. It forces aura to explode while enduring overflow and if he can't beat the opponent, he has to escape in that state.

It was the hardest part for Dox to understand while mastering the 66th. So Dox usually only deployed about 70% of the 66th when using it. The 66th was definitely an excellent technique, but it had a limitation that overflow risk was unavoidable.

Therefore, Dox had believed that the 'mastery' of the 66th lay in aura control that completely eliminated overflow. Reaching a state where there is no risk of overflow no matter when or how far it is deployed, that is the end of the 66th.
'Lowering the stance again here?'
The moment Dox anticipated the final blow, Gill lowered his stance again and returned to the first stance of the 66th.
Then Gill planted both claws into the ground and raised his torso like a roaring beast.
At that moment, Dox understood what the real ending of the 66th was.
'Suicide attack. That was why the 66th was so extreme.'
All the aura that was reverberating inside Gilli's body was converging on the blade of the claw buried in the ground. Just like a volcano in Runekandel.
MacLoran 66th
'Gilli MacLoran.'
When she first thought of the 66th at seventeen, she named it after herself.
And she intended to reveal it if a day comes when she's not exiled from the family, when she gets closer to Dox.
The 66th was made to become Dox's shadow, made in anticipation of a moment when she would have to die to save him one day.

Therefore, Dox completely misunderstood the completion of the 66th. To perfectly complete 'Gilli MacLoran', it wasn't about controlling to avoid aura reflux, but mastering a method to 'use' it. The end of the 66th is to lead the reflux to the end and explode it at once.
However.
Now, Gilli didn't want to die for Dox.
While she still had some affection for MacLoran and Dox, despite being hated so much, the only people she would give her life for now were only her brother, Murakan, and her comrades.
'Your energy is quite fierce, but there's no need to avoid it. The only one who dies when it explodes is you.'
"…This time, you finally won, brother. No, to be precise... even this time… I guess."
'If you swallowed the soul stone I gave, it would have been a bit burdensome power….'
Suddenly, Dox's side was cut and his soul energy gushed out like a stream of blood. Someone who had just infiltrated the battlefield had cut Dox.
In this world, there aren't many people who can successfully surprise a Black Knight.
"Did this flesh want to kill our Strawberry Pie?"
Yona Runekandel.

From the moment Gilli first unveiled the 66th, she had been considering the support of the Nameless. It was about time for the Nameless, assuming he separated from Kinsel and infiltrated the ground, to arrive.
Yona quickly knocked Dox down and stabbed him in the chest. There was no choice but to be instantly knocked down as Yona and Owl ambushed Dox together.
'Argh...!'
In the eyes of Dox, who was bent forward, Gilli, who was kneeling with her claws in the ground, was visible. There was still no grudge to be found in her eyes.
Likewise, there was no sense of victory, just a dumb and gloomy look. A very familiar expression to Dox.
Dox finally understood why Gilli always had that look on her face.
It meant she didn't want to hurt you.
